Republican-held districts have the highest Affordable Care Act enrollment, with millions of families depending on subsidies for affordable health care. Farmers, small business owners, and workers without employer coverage are among those who’d be hit hardest if these credits expire.

Yet Republicans are risking a government shutdown by blocking their renewal – a move that’d drive premiums higher and strip coverage from even more Americans, including hundreds of thousands in #TX28.

What’s more, the Republican claim that undocumented immigrants get ACA subsidies is a false narrative they’ve pushed for years. Federal law since 1996 has barred access for undocumented immigrants to federal health benefits. But that didn’t stop Republicans from pushing the same line to sell the American people on the “One Big Beautiful Bill” earlier this year. They’ve recycled this scare tactic for decades, but when premiums rise, Republicans should ask their own constituents if they’re “illegals.”

That’s why I’ll stand firm and keep fighting to protect affordable care.

In Laredo, I hosted a roundtable on the impacts of the government shutdown across South Texas. We covered how the shutdown is affecting local families, federal employees, veterans, farmers, and small businesses, including the potential doubling of health insurance premiums for 113,000 residents in #TX28 if Affordable Care Act tax credits are not extended.

I addressed and corrected false claims about undocumented immigrants receiving federal health benefits, emphasizing the importance of honest and fact-based dialogue. I also shared that I signed a letter refusing my congressional pay. If nearly 15,000 federal employees in TX-28 are going without a paycheck, then neither will I.

The roundtable brought together several community partners and organizations supporting South Texans during this challenging time. I want to thank Mayor Treviño and everyone who joined the discussion for their insights and commitment to our community. 

A government shutdown doesn’t just affect politicians in Washington – it affects real people in our communities. It impacts families, delays paychecks for federal workers, and disrupts services people rely on. I will continue working with colleagues from both parties to find solutions and ensure stability for the people of South Texas.

As Republicans prolong a government shutdown of their own making, they continue to push the false claim that undocumented immigrants receive federal health benefits – a debate settled under President Bill Clinton in 1996.

This misinformation persists despite decades of clear federal law. @ReichlinMelnick of the @immcouncil  makes it clear: undocumented immigrants are not eligible for Medicaid or ACA subsidies. They cannot get tax credits like American citizens can.

🚨 Due to the Republican shutdown, the federal government remains closed. However, @DeptVetAffairs will continue providing essential care and benefits to veterans and their families.

VA Medical Centers, Outpatient Clinics, and Vet Centers remain open and operational. Benefits such as compensation, pension, education, and housing will continue to be processed and delivered on schedule.

Some services, including transition assistance and public outreach, are paused.

My office will continue to assist South Texas veterans and provide updates throughout the shutdown.

For full details on available VA services, please visit: https://t.co/3Cb0sMkVZG

This morning in Zapata, I toured the Zapata County @GCHCTexas Health Clinic alongside County Judge Joe Rathmell, County Sheriff Ramon Montes, and Precinct 2 Justice of the Peace Judge Olga Bruni with CEO Elmo Lopez to see firsthand the vital services they provide to our community.

After the tour, we discussed how the ongoing government shutdown could affect Gateway’s operations and the thousands of patients who depend on its care. The ripple effects reach far beyond Washington. They touch the lives of South Texans who rely on affordable, accessible health care.

Clinics like Gateway are the backbone of rural health in South Texas. I’ll keep working to end the shutdown, protect health care access, and ensure our clinics have the resources they need to continue serving families across our region.

Today, I joined 143 of my House colleagues in calling on Speaker Johnson to immediately end the Republican-led shutdown and protect Affordable Care Act premium tax credits.

In #TX28, 113,000 residents rely on these credits to afford quality health coverage. Already, some Americans are seeing their costs increase by more than 250%. That’s unacceptable.

With open enrollment just weeks away, we must act now to prevent higher premiums and keep families insured. I’ll continue working in a bipartisan way to reopen the government, lower costs, and protect access to essential care.

Texans are already feeling the impacts of the Republican-led government shutdown.

These are stories from our family, friends, and neighbors.

I’ll continue to share your voices during this shutdown because without action, millions of Americans will face higher costs as health insurance premiums double – and in some cases, triple. I’m fighting to keep costs low, and I always will.

Follow this link to tell me how the shutdown is affecting you and your family in #TX28:
https://t.co/uwWxvlgFwa

Democrats will continue to stand strong in Washington to keep health care costs low, reopen the government, and ensure every federal employee receives their paycheck.

Today, I joined my fellow @HouseDemocrats on the steps of the U.S. Capitol to demand an end to the Republican-led shutdown that’s hurting families across America. Instead of negotiating, Republicans refuse to hold votes, leaving millions without certainty or support.

In South Texas, the stakes couldn’t be higher. More than 55,000 of my constituents are already at risk of losing Medicaid, and another 113,000 will lose affordable coverage if Republicans continue blocking the extension of health care tax credits.

This shutdown is forcing Border Patrol agents, customs officers, and other essential workers in #TX28 to do their jobs without pay. It’s putting veterans at risk of delays in care and cutting off critical assistance to farmers, small businesses, and families.

Democrats remain ready to work across the aisle and deliver a bipartisan solution that lowers costs, protects health care, and gets the government back open.

This afternoon in Poteet, I visited the Poteet Community Federal Health Center and toured the facility to see firsthand the vital services they provide to the community.

During the visit, I had the opportunity to learn more about the center’s programs and how they support families with accessible, quality health care. Clinics like the Poteet Community Health Center are essential to the health and well-being of South Texans.

I’ll continue working to ensure these clinics have the resources they need to serve our communities and help families get the care they deserve.

I met today with Megan K. Williams, @TAMU assistant professor of Health Policy Management, and HPM students Samanvi Chintalapudi and Yulissa Rodriguez – a proud Laredoan – representing @SOPHEtweets.

We discussed the importance of public health, especially in our rural communities, and how preventive medicine keeps families healthy and care accessible across South Texas. Gig ’em!

I joined @ChrisCuomo and my colleague @RepPatHarrigan on @NewsNation to discuss the ongoing shutdown and how we can protect Americans’ access to health care.

The last shutdown was over border wall funding; this one is about health care funding. Once again, the American people are being put in the middle of a political fight that should have been resolved through negotiation. Instead, votes in the House continue to be cancelled.

It’s also unfortunate to see the same myth repeated that illegal immigrants are trying to access federal health benefits. They cannot. That debate has long been settled and distracts from the real issue of keeping our government open and serving families in need.

Here are the facts: of the last nine votes to fund the government, Democrats voted yes with a decisive majority on eight, even when Republicans held the majority in 2024. Republicans were split on all but one. The reality is clear – the government only gets funded when both parties work together.

That’s why negotiation is essential. I’m ready to sit down Monday morning with colleague from North Carolina, Rep. Harrigan, or with any Republican or Democrat, to hammer out an agreement that protects health care and keeps our government working for the American people.

Watch the full segment.⬇️

A constituent recently shared that their monthly health insurance payment will rise from $767.65 in 2025 to $1,069.21 in 2026 – a 39% increase before any subsidies are applied. That’s an unsustainable jump for families trying to make ends meet.

This isn’t an isolated case. More than 113,000 of our neighbors in #TX28 will see premium increases next year, with even higher rate hikes expected. These rising costs are pricing people out of coverage and putting quality care further out of reach.

We can only fix this if Republicans and Democrats come to the negotiating table and work together on real solutions that keep costs low, expand access, and ensure Americans can rely on affordable, quality health care.

I’ve helped secure $17,004,560 in federal funding to expand access to quality health care, upgrade medical facilities, and support health professionals serving families across Webb County.

These investments improve patient care, strengthen local clinics, and ensure our communities have the resources needed to stay healthy.

I’ll continue standing up for South Texas in Congress – ensuring that federal dollars return home to fund projects that strengthen and grow our communities for generations to come.

My San Antonio Outreach Coordinator, Kelly Brooks, attended the groundbreaking ceremony for the first Medical Examiner’s Office in Atascosa County. The new facility will serve multiple counties across the region, strengthening inter-county collaboration and improving the delivery of essential public services.

This project marks a historic partnership among five participating counties and represents a significant step forward in enhancing regional public service infrastructure. I remain committed to supporting initiatives that improve public health and ensure residents of TX-28 have access to vital medical services.

ICYMI: I joined with Republicans and Democrats in sending a letter to @LeaderJohnThune and @SenSchumer urging the Senate to include the House in negotiations on health care reform as Affordable Care Act premium tax credits are set to expire.

Families across South Texas are already seeing higher premium estimates for next year, and millions nationwide could lose their coverage without action. This is not a partisan issue – it’s about keeping health care affordable for working families, small businesses, and seniors.

A bipartisan approach across both chambers is essential to preventing drastic spikes in costs. And when the Senate puts this issue on the floor, the American people deserve a full, fair vote on a plan that keeps health care affordable. I’ll keep working across the aisle to make sure families can keep the care they count on.

My San Antonio Outreach Coordinator, Jesus Toro Martinez, visited the Gateway Community Health Center’s South Laredo Pharmacy to learn more about the essential services the pharmacy team provides to families across the community. During the visit, our office discussed the center’s ongoing work to expand access to affordable medications, strengthen patient support, and serve some of the most vulnerable residents in South Laredo.
 
Gateway Community Health Center continues to play a crucial role in delivering reliable, compassionate care. Their pharmacy team helps patients manage chronic conditions, navigate health resources, and stay connected to the care they need to remain healthy.
 
We’re grateful for the Gateway team’s dedication and the impact they make every day. Our office looks forward to continuing to support their work and partnering on future outreach opportunities for South Laredo families.

Today, I joined colleagues from both sides of the aisle to highlight a bipartisan, common-sense approach to protecting Americans’ health care. I’m grateful to my friends and colleagues @RepJoshG and @RepJenKiggans for bringing us together to focus on meaningful solutions.

For families in South Texas and across the country, health care is not a partisan issue. It’s about being able to see a doctor, fill a prescription, and keep coverage next year. As of today, premiums are set to rise – no ifs, ands, or buts – and the people we represent will feel it first. That’s why we’re working together to lower costs and strengthen access to care, while cutting down on waste, fraud, and abuse. We can do both and we will.

Responsible reform should work for the American people and earn support in both chambers. When Democrats and Republicans come to the table, we not only protect working families, we also restore trust in the idea that Congress can still deliver real results.

I look forward to continuing this bipartisan effort to ensure every community has access to affordable, reliable health care. Our country counts on us to choose cooperation over conflict and service over showmanship. May we meet that responsibility with steady hands and good faith as we fight for those we serve.

I am excited to share that @RegionOneESC has been awarded $1,198,055 through the @usedgov Mental Health Service Professionals Demonstration Program. This grant will support innovative partnerships to train school counselors, social workers, psychologists, and other mental health professionals, expanding access to mental health services in low-income K–12 schools.

By addressing the shortage of school-based mental health professionals, this program will help students receive the care and support they need to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. I will keep fighting to ensure our schools have the resources and professionals necessary to support every student’s mental health and success.

We are in the holiday season, and families across the country are feeling the pressure of rising costs. Everyday Americans are seeing prices climb in real time, from groceries to gifts to health care.

New reports show the average family has already paid hundreds more this year because of higher costs, with even higher expenses expected ahead. Popular holiday gifts are significantly more expensive than last year, and many families are buying fewer presents or stretching every dollar just to get by.

Small businesses and working people are feeling this strain as well. Layoffs are rising, health insurance premiums are increasing, and millions of workers and self-employed Americans are facing uncertainty at a time when stability matters most.

Affordability is not a talking point. It is a real challenge for families trying to make ends meet. I am fighting for affordable prices for families, because no one should struggle to enjoy the holidays or provide for their loved ones.

As the year comes to a close, I’m proud to highlight the results my team and I delivered for #TX28 – from returning more than $1.7 million directly to constituents to securing billions in federal investments for education, infrastructure, public safety, border security, health care, job creation, and more. Looking ahead to 2026, I will continue working in a bipartisan way to deliver practical results that strengthen our communities and keep South Texas moving forward.
